Imperative forms show no subject-pronoun agreement; they address tu, nous, or vous only.

patches.entity_key: No futur simple after 'si' in future condition
value: Each clause keeps its own subject-verb agreement; the si clause uses the present tense instead of the futur simple.
si is an invariable conjunction and triggers no agreement change.

evidence.notes: Tense restriction after si does not alter subject-verb agreement in either clause. AI-generated, unverified.

patches.entity_key: Other negations (personne, jamais, plus, rien, guère)
value: The negative particles personne, jamais, plus, rien, and guère are invariable.
When personne or rien is the subject, the verb agrees with it in the third-person singular (Personne n'est venu).

evidence.notes: Particles are invariable; personne/rien as subject take a third-person singular verb. AI-generated, unverified.

value: où is invariable and does not agree in gender or number with its antecedent.
Unlike lequel, où carries no gender or number marking.

evidence.notes: où is an invariable relative adverb/pronominal form used for place. AI-generated, unverified.

value: où is invariable when the antecedent expresses time; it marks no gender or number agreement.
The time antecedent (année, jour, instant, siècle) transfers no agreement to où.

evidence.notes: Temporal où remains invariable (l'année où, le jour où). AI-generated, unverified.

value: In the negative, du/de la/de l'/des all become invariable de (d' before a vowel), so the article no longer shows gender or number.
After être the partitive article remains and keeps its gender and number agreement (Ce n'est pas du fromage).

evidence.notes: Matches the rule's stated être exception; de after negation is invariable. AI-generated, unverified.

value: In compound tenses the past participle agrees in gender and number with the subject (Ces livres se sont bien vendus).

patches.entity_key: Passive used to avoid specifying agent
value: The past participle agrees in gender and number with the subject of the passive sentence.
Omitting the agent (par + noun) does not affect participle agreement with the subject.
